Defined in `lib.animation`.


Open with ``from_bbmodel()``, declare clips with ``animation()``, delete
with ``remove_animation()`` and persist with ``save()``. Clips the recipe

## `IKReport`

Defined in `lib.ik`.

```python
class IKReport(chain: 'tuple[str, ...]', samples: 'int', max_error: 'float', unit: 'str', unreachable: 'tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]', limited: 'tuple[str, ...]', ok: 'bool') -> None
```

Outcome of one ``reach``/``aim`` bake.

``max_error`` is the largest tip-to-target distance in model units (``reach``) or the largest
angle in degrees between the aimed axis and the target (``aim``). ``unreachable`` lists the time
intervals where the target was farther than the chain can stretch, ``limited`` the controls whose
rotation limits clamped the solution. ``ok`` is true when every sample met the tolerance.

## `PathSection`

Defined in `lib.procedural`.

```python
class PathSection(name: str, profile: lib.procedural.Profile, at: float | None = None, point: int | None = None, rotation: float = 0.0, offset: tuple = (0.0, 0.0), distance: float | None = None) -> None
```

A named cross-section along a ``Path3D`` (used by ``add_sweep(sections=...)``).

``at`` is the arc-length distance from the first path point; values
before 0 or past the end extend straight along the end directions.
``point`` instead places the section exactly on path vertex ``point``
(its frame bisects the bend there).  The section name becomes a mesh
anchor and ring, so bones can target ``"mesh:name"``.

## `SurfaceContact`

Defined in `lib.spatial`.

```python
class SurfaceContact(origin: tuple = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), normal: tuple = (0.0, 1.0, 0.0), tangent_u: tuple | None = None, tangent_v: tuple | None = None) -> None
```

An oriented point on an outer surface.

``normal`` always points out of the owning geometry.  ``tangent_u`` and
``tangent_v`` are an orthonormal, right-handed basis of the contact plane:
``cross(tangent_u, tangent_v) == normal``.  This is deliberately distinct
from :class:`SpatialFrame`: an attachment needs a surface normal, while a
generic socket only has a forward/up convention.

Supplying no tangents chooses a deterministic world-aligned basis.  A
caller may supply either tangent to preserve a meaningful seam direction;
supplying both is accepted only when they describe the same oriented
contact plane.


### Members

- `as_spatial_frame(self)` — Adapt this contact to a SpatialFrame convention with forward along normal.

- `frame` (property) — A conventional frame whose Z axis is the outward normal.

Linear per-vertex weight factor: 1 at ``t=0`` falling to 0 at ``t>=1`` (clamped).

## `periodic`

Defined in `lib.motion`.

```python
def periodic(samples: 'Sequence', period: 'float') -> 'Callable[[float], object]'
```

Function of time interpolating evenly spaced ``samples`` (numbers or 3-vectors) over one ``period``,
repeating outside it. ``samples[i]`` is the value at ``i * period / len(samples)``.


## `periodic_curve`

Defined in `lib.motion`.

```python
def periodic_curve(keys: 'Sequence[tuple[float, float]]', x: 'float') -> 'float'
```

Value at ``x`` of a looping curve through ``(x, value)`` keys with x in [0, 1).

The curve has continuous value and slope everywhere, including across the loop. Its slope is zero
at keys that are plateaus or turning points, so it never overshoots between keys: a value held
between two equal keys stays exactly there.


## `quintic`

Defined in `lib.motion`.

```python
def quintic(p0: 'float', p1: 'float', v0: 'float', v1: 'float', s: 'float') -> 'float'
```

Value going from ``p0`` (s = 0) to ``p1`` (s = 1) with slopes ``v0`` and ``v1`` (per unit of s)
and no acceleration at either end.

Use it to join two phases of a motion without a jolt: pass each phase's speed at the joint,
multiplied by the duration that ``s`` spans.


## `smooth_falloff`

Defined in `lib.spatial`.

```python
def smooth_falloff(t)
```

Smooth (smoothstep) per-vertex weight factor over the ``linear_falloff`` range.


## `smooth_periodic`

Defined in `lib.motion`.

```python
def smooth_periodic(samples: 'Sequence', period: 'float', seconds: 'float') -> 'list'
```

``samples`` (numbers or 3-vectors) evenly spaced over one ``period``, blurred by a Gaussian of
``seconds`` (one standard deviation) that wraps around the loop. Softens corners in a repeating curve
without moving its mean. Returns the blurred samples as a list; pass it to ``periodic`` for a
function of time.


## `spring_follow`

Defined in `lib.motion`.

```python
def spring_follow(target: 'Callable[[float], tuple]', frequency: 'float', damping: 'float', period: 'float', *, rate: 'int' = 240, cycles: 'int' = 3) -> 'Callable[[float], tuple]'
```

A point pulled toward ``target(t)`` by a damped spring, for a motion repeating every ``period``.

The spring is simulated for ``cycles`` periods so it settles into its repeating motion, and the last
one is returned as a looping function of time. ``frequency`` (Hz) sets how quickly it catches up and
``damping`` (1 = no overshoot) how much it swings past. Use it to make a point trail another with
inertia, then aim or reach a control at it.
